facts.fact: H. Chandler Egan, 1918 (club card); a City of Portland course.
It borders the Crystal Springs Rhododendron Garden.
Crystal Springs Creek flows through the course; coho, chinook and steelhead use it.

current.subject: A pink rhododendron truss over its leaves.
current.keep: The rhododendron, for the garden next door.
current.weaknesses: Side-on truss and leaves read as a pink blob on green.

concepts.name: The Rhododendron Rosette
concepts.rationale: Seen from above, the way the game sees everything: a dome of pink bells inside a whorl of glossy leaves.
concepts.symbolism: The garden next door, in full May bloom.
concepts.strengths: A crisp radial emblem; reads at 1x.
concepts.tradeoffs: Flowers are common in park graphics.

concepts.name: Salmon in the City
concepts.rationale: A coho in spawning colours leaping from the creek. Salmon still run through the middle of a city golf course.
references: Crystal Springs Creek and its salmon (fact)
concepts.symbolism: A wild river running through a public course in the city.
concepts.tradeoffs: A leaping fish is a familiar Northwest motif.

recommendation: Concept 1. The top-down rosette is the most refined version of a subject the course owns; the salmon is a strong second for conservation messaging.
